questions.question: Where does the East Coast of India lie?

options.text: Between Gulf of Cambay and Cape Comorin
Between Eastern Ghats and the Bay of Bengal

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The East Coast of India lies between the Eastern Ghats mountain range and the Bay of Bengal.**
 
• **The Eastern Ghats, also known as the Mahendra Range**, is a discontinuous mountain range that runs parallel to the **East Coast of India**.
 
• It stretches along the states of** Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Tamil Nadu**.
 
• **The East Coast plains, **which lie between the** Eastern Ghats and the Bay of Bengal, **are relatively flat and fertile, making them suitable for agriculture.
 
• This region is home to several major cities and important ports along the coast.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Between the Gulf of Cambay and Cape Comorin lies the western coast of India, also known as the West Coast of India.**

 
 
• The West Coast of India is situated along the** Arabian Sea and extends from the Gulf of Cambay (also known as the Gulf of Khambhat) in the north to Cape Comorin (also known as Kanyakumari) in the south.**
 
• This coastal stretch includes the states of **Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, and Kerala.**
 
• **The West Coast of India** is known for its** beautiful beaches, diverse culture, and important port cities such as Mumbai, Mangalore, Kochi, and Thiruvananthapuram.**
 
 
 
• **Between Maharashtra and Kerala lies the state of Karnataka.**
 
 
• Karnataka is located on the southwestern part of India and shares its borders with **Maharashtra to the north and Kerala to the south.**
 
• The state capital of Karnataka is Bengaluru (Bangalore), which is known as the **technology hub of India.**
 
• Karnataka is known for its** rich cultural heritage, historical sites, and natural beauty**.
 
• It is also home to several important cities and tourist destinations, including **Mysore, Hampi, Mangalore, and Coorg.**
 
 
 
• **​Between Diu and Kerala lies the state of Gujarat and the Union Territory of Daman and Diu.**
 
 
• **Diu** is a small island and town located off the southern coast of **Gujarat, while Kerala is situated on the southwestern tip of India.**
 
• **To travel from Diu to Kerala, **one would need to traverse the state of **Gujarat, pass through Maharashtra, and then enter Kerala.**
 
• The journey would involve traveling along the western coast of India.

questions.question: If ex ante aggregate demand and ex ante aggregate supply are plotted together in a graphical diagram, then at which point equilibrium will be reached?

options.text: Where ex ante aggregate demand is less than ex ante aggregate supply
Where ex ante aggregate demand is equal to ex ante aggregate supply
Where ex ante aggregate demand is more than ex ante aggregate supply
Where ex ante aggregate demand is zero

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__**.** 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** In a graphical diagram where ex ante aggregate demand (AD) and ex ante aggregate supply (AS) are plotted together, equilibrium is reached at the point where the two curves intersect.**
 
• This intersection represents the level of real output and price level where** the quantity of goods and services demanded (AD) is equal to the quantity supplied (AS).**
 
• **At this equilibrium point**, there is no tendency for the economy to move away from it, as the quantity demanded matches the quantity supplied.
 
• **The equilibrium point** can be thought of as the point of balance in the economy, where there is no excess demand or excess supply.
 
• It is where **buyers' and sellers' **plans align, resulting in a stable state in which the economy is in equilibrium.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **In an economy, demand and supply refer to the forces that determine the quantity** **of goods and services exchanged in the market. **

 
 
• **Demand: **Demand represents the quantity of goods and services that buyers are willing and able to purchase at various price levels, during a specific period.

 
 
• Demand is influenced by factors such as price, consumer preferences, income levels, population, and the availability of substitutes.
 
• The relationship between price and quantity demanded is typically inverse, meaning that as the price increases, the quantity demanded tends to decrease, and vice versa.
 
• Demand is usually represented by a downward-sloping demand curve.
 
 
 
• **Supply: **Supply, on the other hand, represents the quantity of goods and services that sellers are willing and able to offer for sale at different price levels.
 
 
• The supply is influenced by factors such as production costs, technology, resource availability, government regulations, and expectations of future prices.
 
• The relationship between price and quantity supplied is usually positive, meaning that as the price increases, the quantity supplied tends to increase, and vice versa.
 
• Supply is often represented by an upward-sloping supply curve.
 
 
 
• **The interaction of demand and supply determines** **the equilibrium price** **and quantity in a market.**
 
 
• When the quantity demanded equals the quantity supplied, the market is said to be in equilibrium.
 
• Changes in demand or supply will shift the respective curves, leading to changes in the equilibrium price and quantity.
 
• For example, an increase in demand will shift the demand curve to the right, leading to a higher equilibrium price and quantity.
 
 
 
 
 
• Understanding the dynamics of demand and supply is crucial in analyzing market behavior, price fluctuations, and the allocation of resources in an economy.

questions.question: Which law is also known as the law of inertia?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The law that is also known as the law of inertia is Newton's First Law of Motion.**
 
• It states that an object at rest tends to **stay at rest, and an object in motion tends to stay in motion with the same speed and in the same direction unless acted upon by an external force.**
 
• This fundamental law of **physics was formulated by Sir Isaac Newton** and is one of the three laws that form the basis of classical mechanics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Newton's Second Law of Motion, also known as the law of acceleration, describes the relationship between the force acting on an object, the mass of the object, and the resulting acceleration.**

 
 
• It is one of the fundamental principles of classical mechanics formulated by Sir Isaac Newton.
 
 
 
• **Archimedes' principle states that when an object is placed in a fluid (like water), it experiences an upward force called buoyant force.**
 
 
• This force is equal to the weight of the fluid that the object displaces (pushes aside).
 
• 
 
**Example - **when you put something in water, it feels a push from the water that tries to lift it up. The more water the object pushes away, the stronger the push (buoyant force) it feels. If the object is lighter than the water it displaces, it will float because the buoyant force is greater than the weight of the object. If the object is heavier, it will sink because the weight is greater than the buoyant force.

 
 
 
 
• **Kepler's laws are a set of three fundamental principles that describe the motion of planets and other celestial objects around the Sun. **Here's a simplified explanation of each law:
 
 
• **Law of Orbits:** Each planet in our solar system moves around the Sun in an elliptical orbit, with the Sun at one of the two foci of the ellipse. In simpler terms, the path of a planet is not a perfect circle but more like a stretched-out circle with the Sun slightly off-center.
 
• **Law of Areas: **An imaginary line connecting a planet to the Sun sweeps out equal areas in equal time intervals. In other words, as a planet moves in its elliptical orbit, it covers an equal area in space over equal periods of time. This means that a planet moves faster when it is closer to the Sun and slower when it is farther away.
 
• **Law of Periods: **The square of the time period of a planet's orbit is proportional to the cube of its average distance from the Sun. In simpler terms, the time it takes for a planet to complete one orbit around the Sun (its period) is related to its average distance from the Sun. The farther a planet is from the Sun, the longer its orbital period.

questions.question: Sher Khan defeated Humayun at Kanauj in the year ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Option 2**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sher Shah Suri defeated Humayun at the Battle of Kanauj in the year 1540.**
 
• The battle took place near the city of **Kanauj, located in present-day Uttar Pradesh, India**.
 
• Sher Shah Suri's forces, under his leadership, emerged victorious in this battle, resulting in Humayun's temporary expulsion from the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Humayun was able to regain his empire later and reclaim Delhi in 1555.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sher Shah Suri was born in 1486 in Sasaram, present-day Bihar, India.**

 
 
• He belonged to the Pashtun Sur tribe, hence the name **"Suri."**
 
• **Sher Shah Suri** initially served under the **Delhi Sultanate** and later joined the service of the **Mughal emperor Humayun.**
 
 
 
• **​Humayun, also known as Nasir-ud-Din Muhammad Humayun, was the second Mughal emperor who ruled over a significant portion of the Indian subcontinent.**
 
 
• He was born on **March 6, 1508,** in **Kabul, Afghanistan, and he ascended to the throne in 1530.**
 
• Humayun was the **eldest son of the first Mughal emperor, Babur.**
 
• During his reign, he faced several **challenges, including conflicts with regional rulers and internal power struggles.**
 
• Humayun's reign was marked by ups and downs, as he lost and regained his empire multiple times.

questions.question:
Which of the following pairs of 'disease – duration' is correct?

I. Acute – long duration

II. Chronic – short time
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The correct pairing of 'disease - duration' is:
 
 
• **Acute - short time**
 
• ** Chronic - long duration**
 
 
 
• **Acute diseases** are characterized by a sudden onset and a relatively short duration. They typically resolve within a short period, ranging from a few days to a few weeks. Examples of acute diseases include the common cold, acute bronchitis, and acute appendicitis.
 
• On the other hand, **chronic diseases** are characterized by a long duration, typically lasting for months or years. They often develop slowly and persist over an extended period, sometimes for a person's lifetime. Examples of chronic diseases include diabetes, hypertension (high blood pressure), and rheumatoid arthritis.
 
• Therefore, the correct pairing would be **"Acute - short time" and "Chronic - long duration."**

questions.question: Which part of the Indian Constitution is related with the Fundamental rights?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Part III of the Constitution__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Fundamental Rights (FRs) are known as the base of the Indian constitution & mentioned in Part III of the constitution.
 
• They prohibit unreasonable interference of the state & prevent its executive & legislature to become authoritarian, hence put due limitations of state power.
 
• Observance of fundamental duties is required for having one’s FRs redressed in case of their violation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/292e0c96dd6c006ce1f3ef21b86308c7c73a2bc69f508d641b46f352d114f429.png] Important Points__

__
 
• FRs are not absolute but qualified rights.
 
• It is Subject to certain restrictions imposed by the state on the question of national security, interest & general welfare of the society.
 
• But restrictions are checked by SC & HCs, whether restrictions are reasonable or not.
 
• SC verdict in the Golaknath V/S state of Punjab (1967) - FRs have been given a transcendental position by constitution hence no authority functioning under the constitution including parliament has the power to amend FRs.
 
• In Keshavananda Bharati V/S state of Kerala, 1973, SC held that parliament has the power to amend any provision of the constitution including part III, however, parliament’s amending power subjects to the “Basic structure of the constitution".​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

There are six Fundamental Rights-

 
 

 Article 14 – 18
 Right to Equality
 
 

 Article 19-22
 Right to Freedom
 
 

 Article 23-24
 Right against Exploitation
 
 

 Article 25-28
 Right to Freedom of Religion
 
 

 Article 29-30
 Cultural & Education Rights
 
 

 Article 32
 Right to Constitutional Remedies

questions.question: The concept of “Procedure Established by Law” in the Indian constitution is borrowed from which of the following countries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Japan__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• It means that a law has been duly enacted by the competent body following the correct procedure. For example, the procedure mentioned in the constitution.
 
• The Doctrine of Procedure established by law has been taken from the Japanese Constitution.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The Indian constitution came into force on 26th January 1950.
 
• It was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26th November 1949. 
 
• Some provisions of the Constitution pertaining to citizenship, elections, provisional parliament, and temporary and transitional provisions.
 
• And short title contained in Articles 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 60, 324, 366, 367, 379, 380, 388, 391, 392 and 393 came into force on November 26, 1949,.
 
• The remaining provisions (the major part) of the Constitution came into force on January 26, 1950.
 
• This day is referred to in the Constitution as the date of its commencement and is celebrated as Republic Day.
 
• January 26 was specifically chosen as the date of commencement of the Constitution because of its historical importance.
 
• It was on this day in 1930 that Purna Swaraj day was celebrated, following the resolution of the Lahore Session (December 1929) of the INC.

questions.question: ______ serves as the entry and exit point of a network, as all data coming in or going out of a network must first pass through it in order to use routing paths.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gateway**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A gateway serves as the entry and exit point of a network. It acts as a communication point or interface between different networks, allowing data to pass through it in order to use routing paths.
 
• Gateways are responsible for protocol translation, security enforcement, and network traffic management.
 
• They can connect networks that use different protocols, such as connecting a local area network (LAN) to the internet.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• Network Interface: A gateway is equipped with multiple network interfaces to connect different networks. It can have connections to the internet, local area networks (LANs), wide area networks (WANs), or other networks.
 
• Protocol Translation: Gateways are responsible for translating protocols between different networks. They can convert data packets from one protocol to another, allowing communication between networks that use different standards or languages.
 
• Traffic Routing: When data enters a network, it must pass through the gateway. The gateway examines the packet's destination address and determines the best routing path for the data to reach its intended destination. It helps direct traffic efficiently within the network or between different networks.
 
• Network Address Translation (NAT): Gateways often perform Network Address Translation, which allows multiple devices on a LAN to share a single public IP address. It masks the private IP addresses of devices behind the gateway's public IP address, enhancing security and conserving IP addresses.

questions.question: Which of the following factors of soil formation determines the accumulation of the soil?
questions.solution:
**The Correct answer is: Parent rock**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **Parent Rock:**

 
 
• This is the **correct factor** that determines the accumulation of soil.
 
• The parent rock provides the **basic mineral composition** of the soil.
 
• Its nature (hard, soft, coarse-grained, or fine-grained) influences the **rate of weathering** and the type of soil formed.
 
• Soils derived from granite are sandy, while basalt produces black cotton soil rich in clay.
 
 
 
• **Fauna:**
 
 
• Animals, insects, and microorganisms help in mixing organic matter and improving soil aeration.
 
• They aid in soil fertility but do not determine the accumulation of the soil itself.
 
 
 
• **Flora:**
 
 
• Plants add humus and organic matter to the soil.
 
• They enrich the soil but do not decide the fundamental accumulation of soil material.
 
 
 
• **Relief:**
 
 
• Relief (slope and altitude) influences drainage and erosion.
 
• It affects soil depth and moisture but is not the primary determinant of accumulation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Factors of Soil Formation:**

 
 
• **Parent rock** – source of mineral matter.
 
• **Climate** – temperature and rainfall affect weathering and humus content.
 
• **Organisms** – flora and fauna add organic matter.
 
• **Relief** – slope and drainage determine soil depth and erosion.
 
• **Time** – longer duration allows mature soil profiles to develop.
 
 
 
• **Example:**
 
 
• Alluvial soils in India are deposited by rivers and depend on the parent rock material carried from the Himalayas.
 
• Black soil of the Deccan Plateau is derived from basaltic parent rock.

questions.question: Majuli is a river island in the Brahmaputra River in which of the following states of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Assam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Majuli is a large river island situated in the middle of the Brahmaputra River in Assam.

 
 
• Majuli is depicted as the largest river island in the world.
 
• This island has been formed over a period of time due to the change of direction and area of the Brahmaputra river and its tributaries especially the Lohit river.
 
• Majuli can also be called the 'cultural capital of Assam'.
 
• Majuli is located in the northern part of the Jorhat district and is separated from the mainland by the Brahmaputra river.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• Brahmaputra River flows through Tibet, India and Bangladesh.

 
 
• The Brahmaputra rises in the north of the Himalayas near Lake Mansarovar in the Purang district of Tibet, where it is known as the Yarlung Tsangpo.
 
• Flowing in Tibet, this river enters the Indian state of Arunachal Pradesh.
 
• Flowing in the valley of Assam, it is called the Brahmaputra, and then it is called Jamuna as soon as it enters Bangladesh.​

questions.question: Who among the following started the Kuka Movement?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Satguru Ram Singh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• After the fall of the kingdom of Maharaja Ranjit Singh, there were several attempts to raise the old glory of the Khalsa.
 
• Several movements to reform the Sikhism were started.
 
• First, one being the Namdhari movement, which was started by Baba Ram Singh Namdhari after Anglo Sikh wars.
 
• He was a soldier in the Khalsa army.
 
• Like the Nirankari, this second reform movement known as the Namdhari, or Kuka, movement also had its origin in the north-west corner of the Sikh kingdom, away from the places of royal pomp and grandeur.
 
• It harked back to a way of life more in keeping with the spiritual tradition of the community.
 
• Its principal object was to spread the true spirit of Sikhism shorn of tawdry customs and mannerism, which had been growing on it since the beginning of the Sikh monarchy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In the midst of national pride born of military glory and political power, this movement extolled the religious obligation for pious and simple living.
 
• They were called "Kukas" because of their particular style to recite the Gurbani (Sayings of the Gurus).
 
• This style was in a high pitched voice, called Kook in Punjabi, and thus Namdhari Khalsa’s were named Kukas.
 
• In the post-1857 phase of the freedom struggle, the Namdhari movement occupies a very significant place in the annals of history.
 
• It was founded at a time when the socio-religious teachings of the great Gurus were slowly being shadowed by other considerations and the political life was at its lowest ebb.
 
• Namdhari movement was an offshoot of Sikhism.
 
• The Kuka Movement was launched on the Baisakhi day in April 1857 at Bhaini (sahib), in Ludhiana District of Punjab.
 
• The leader of the Namdhari movement Baba Ram Singh was inspired by Maharaj Singh’s struggle against aliens and worked for social reforms and gave a call for the political battle against the Britishers.

questions.question: By which of the following process can we separate two miscible liquids?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Distillation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Distillation **

 
 
• It Separates a mixture of two miscible liquids (Miscible liquids are one that together when mixed, form a homogenous mixture whose composition is the same throughout.) 
 
• A liquid mixture's components are vaporized, condensed, and then separated here.
 
• As the mixture is heated, the volatile component vaporizes first.
 
• The vapour is deposited in a liquid state after passing through a condenser. 
 
• EXAMPLE - separation of gasoline from crude oil, formation of freshwater from salt-water. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Law of Demand states that, there is a negative relationship between ______.

options.text: tax on a commodity and its price
demand for a commodity and its supply
demand for a commodity and its price
supply of a commodity and its price

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**demand for a commodity and its price**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• According to the law of demand

 
 
• ​​​​when the price of a commodity increase, its the quantity demanded decreases
 
• when the price of a commodity decreases, it’s the quantity demanded increases
 
• keeping other factors remains the same.
 
 
 
• The consumer’s demand for good must be inversely related to the price of the good.
 
• There is an inverse relationship between price and demand and due to this the demand curve always has a downward slope.
 
• Demand Curve is the relation between the quantity of the good chosen by a consumer and the price of the good.
 
• ​Assumptions for the Law of Demand
 
 
• ​​No change in the income of consumers 
 
• No change is the taste and preference of the consumers 
 
• No change in price related to other goods.
